changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: One global type list for every holding kind (issue #479). Each type declares the kinds it applies to. Stock types are copied with kinds {STOCKS} and fund types with {FUNDS}, both keeping their external_id so ids the client cached stay valid; a fund type whose name a stock type already uses becomes "name (fundo)", so filtering by type label returns exactly the holdings it did before. A "Cripto" type is seeded for the existing crypto holdings. The rollback drops the table; the copies are rebuilt from it by 24-1000-5's rollback.

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: Point every holding at its holding_types row, matched through the external_id the copy kept. Stocks and funds always had a type, so the column is required there. Crypto stays nullable: a fresh install has no crypto type until an admin creates one, and a required type would block adding crypto until then.

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: The stock segment list becomes the segment list of every kind. The views follow the renames on their own, since Postgres tracks them by OID. Rolling back drops every fund and crypto segment, which cannot be kept without the columns.

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: holdings_overview reads type_label from holding_types and segment_label from segments for every kind; crypto LEFT JOINs the type because its type is optional. Every column keeps its name, type and position, so holdings_report_rows, holdings_valued and wallet_totals, which read it by column name, need no change. The rollback restores the definition 06-1000-add-owner-wallet-and-gain-to-holdings-overview left, written against the segment names 24-1000-3's rollback renames back afterwards.
changeSet.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW finances.holdings_overview AS SELECT holdings.holding_id, holdings.external_id, holdings.wallet_id, holdings.kind, holdings.status, holdings.name, holdings.ticker, holdings.type_label, holdings.current_price, holdings.quantity, holdings.cost_basis, holdings.current_value, holdings.frozen, holdings.segment_label, holdings.user_id, holdings.wallet_external_id, holdings.wallet_name, holdings.wallet_currency, holdings.current_value - holdings.cost_basis AS gain, CASE WHEN holdings.cost_basis <> 0 THEN ROUND((holdings.current_value - holdings.cost_basis) / holdings.cost_basis, 10) * 100 END AS gain_pct FROM ( SELECT stock_holdings.id AS holding_id, stock_holdings.external_id, stock_holdings.wallet_id, 'STOCKS'::finances.wallet_kind AS kind, stock_holdings.status, stock_holdings.name, stock_holdings.ticker, holding_types.name AS type_label, stock_holdings.current_price, COALESCE(SUM(stock_lots.quantity), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.quantity), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.stock_holding_id = stock_holdings.id ) AS quantity, COALESCE(SUM(stock_lots.quantity * stock_lots.price), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.cost_basis), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.stock_holding_id = stock_holdings.id ) AS cost_basis, stock_holdings.current_price * ( COALESCE(SUM(stock_lots.quantity), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.quantity), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.stock_holding_id = stock_holdings.id ) ) AS current_value, stock_holdings.frozen, segments.name AS segment_label, wallets.user_id, wallets.external_id AS wallet_external_id, wallets.name AS wallet_name, wallets.currency AS wallet_currency FROM finances.stock_holdings JOIN finances.wallets ON wallets.id = stock_holdings.wallet_id JOIN finances.holding_types ON holding_types.id = stock_holdings.holding_type_id LEFT JOIN finances.segments ON segments.id = stock_holdings.segment_id LEFT JOIN finances.stock_lots ON stock_lots.stock_holding_id = stock_holdings.id GROUP BY stock_holdings.id, stock_holdings.external_id, stock_holdings.wallet_id, stock_holdings.status, stock_holdings.name, stock_holdings.ticker, holding_types.name, stock_holdings.current_price, stock_holdings.frozen, wallets.id, segments.name
UNION ALL
SELECT crypto_holdings.id AS holding_id, crypto_holdings.external_id, crypto_holdings.wallet_id, 'CRYPTO'::finances.wallet_kind AS kind, crypto_holdings.status, crypto_holdings.name, crypto_holdings.ticker, holding_types.name AS type_label, crypto_holdings.current_price, COALESCE(SUM(crypto_lots.quantity), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.quantity), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.crypto_holding_id = crypto_holdings.id ) AS quantity, COALESCE(SUM(crypto_lots.quantity * crypto_lots.price), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.cost_basis), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.crypto_holding_id = crypto_holdings.id ) AS cost_basis, crypto_holdings.current_price * ( COALESCE(SUM(crypto_lots.quantity), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.quantity), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.crypto_holding_id = crypto_holdings.id ) ) AS current_value, crypto_holdings.frozen, segments.name AS segment_label, wallets.user_id, wallets.external_id AS wallet_external_id, wallets.name AS wallet_name, wallets.currency AS wallet_currency FROM finances.crypto_holdings JOIN finances.wallets ON wallets.id = crypto_holdings.wallet_id LEFT JOIN finances.holding_types ON holding_types.id = crypto_holdings.holding_type_id LEFT JOIN finances.segments ON segments.id = crypto_holdings.segment_id LEFT JOIN finances.crypto_lots ON crypto_lots.crypto_holding_id = crypto_holdings.id GROUP BY crypto_holdings.id, crypto_holdings.external_id, crypto_holdings.wallet_id, crypto_holdings.status, crypto_holdings.name, crypto_holdings.ticker, holding_types.name, crypto_holdings.current_price, crypto_holdings.frozen, wallets.id, segments.name
UNION ALL
SELECT fund_holdings.id AS holding_id, fund_holdings.external_id, fund_holdings.wallet_id, 'FUNDS'::finances.wallet_kind AS kind, fund_holdings.status, fund_holdings.name, NULL::TEXT AS ticker, holding_types.name AS type_label, NULL::NUMERIC AS current_price, NULL::NUMERIC AS quantity, COALESCE(SUM(fund_contributions.amount), 0) - ( SELECT COALESCE(SUM(results.cost_basis), 0) FROM finances.results WHERE results.fund_holding_id = fund_holdings.id ) AS cost_basis, fund_holdings.current_value, fund_holdings.frozen, segments.name AS segment_label, wallets.user_id, wallets.external_id AS wallet_external_id, wallets.name AS wallet_name, wallets.currency AS wallet_currency FROM finances.fund_holdings JOIN finances.wallets ON wallets.id = fund_holdings.wallet_id JOIN finances.holding_types ON holding_types.id = fund_holdings.holding_type_id LEFT JOIN finances.segments ON segments.id = fund_holdings.segment_id LEFT JOIN finances.fund_contributions ON fund_contributions.fund_holding_id = fund_holdings.id GROUP BY fund_holdings.id, fund_holdings.external_id, fund_holdings.wallet_id, fund_holdings.status, fund_holdings.name, holding_types.name, fund_holdings.current_value, fund_holdings.frozen, wallets.id, segments.name ) AS holdings;

changeSet.author: ${claude}
changeSet.comment: Drop the kind-specific type columns and tables now that no view reads them. Without CASCADE, so any dependent object left behind fails the migration instead of vanishing. The rollback is lossy by nature: it rebuilds stock_types from the types whose kinds contain STOCKS and fund_types from those containing FUNDS with the " (fundo)" suffix stripped, both keeping the external_id, and repoints the holdings through it. Types that only apply to crypto, the seeded "Cripto" included, have nowhere to go back to.
